en: The *Sarvatathāgata-saddharma-rahasya-peṭaka-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
translated at the Indrālaya Temple in the kingdom of Uḍḍiyāna, North India.
Translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of the Dharma, the Purple-Robed Śramaṇa Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree. Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Magadha, within the Vimalārāma (Stainless Garden) beside the Ratnaprabhāsa-taḍāga (Jewel Radiance Pond).
Together with great bodhisattvas and various śrāvakas,
as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
He was surrounded by hundreds of thousands of kings, elders, and householders, who listened to the Dharma with reverence.
At that time, there was a wealthy brāhmaṇa within the assembly.
Named Vimalaprabhā, she was able within that assembly to understand the subtle and profound, was thoroughly versed in the teachings of the Master,
possessed brilliant eloquence, and delighted in extensive learning.
They practiced and honored the ten wholesome actions and placed their trust and reverence in the Triple Gem.
With joy and exultation, they formed this thought:
"All sentient beings take the cultivation of goodness as their cause."
"I shall cultivate immeasurable wealth and abundant provisions.
At that time, the great brahmin Vimalaprabha...
Rising and joining their palms, they circumambulated the Buddha seven times.
They made offerings to the World-Honored One with various flowers, unguents, and powdered incense,
as well as robes, pearls, and necklaces.
Worth hundreds of thousands [of coins], he offered it to the Buddha.
Prostrating with his head at the Buddha’s feet, he said to the Buddha:
"World-Honored One, I pray that you will give rise to great compassion and accept this food from me."
Thus he requested three times.
At that time, the World-Honored One silently accepted the invitation.
Thereupon, the great brahmin Vimalaprabha—
Seeing that the World-Honored One had accepted his invitation by remaining silent,
he quickly returned and spent one night preparing a vast variety of offerings.
Having prepared exquisite food and drink endowed with the six flavors,
he adorned his house, pavilions, and bathing pools with a great abundance of silken fabrics.
There were flowers, powdered incense, various types of incense, and ointments for anointing the body.
All the requisites for offering were fully prepared without exception.
At that moment, the brahmins and others took up flowered banners and performed various kinds of music.
Accompanied by his retinue, he went to the side of the Jewel Radiance Pond within the Immaculate Garden to invite the World-Honored One.
Having arrived, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, the time for the meal has come; the food is all prepared."
"I only pray that the World-Honored One, together with the great assembly,
will come to my home to accept my offerings.
At that time, the World-Honored One surveyed the gathered multitude.
He comforted the great brahmin Vimalaprabha, saying, "Excellent, excellent! It shall be as you have wished.
He further commanded the assembly and all the other devas, "Go all together to that place."
Thereupon, the World-Honored One rose from his seat,
together with the great assembly of bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, devas, nāgas,
the eight classes of supernatural beings, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
Together with the assembly of kings, ministers, subjects, and retinues—
all surrounded by hundreds of thousands who paid him respectful homage—
they all gathered and set out for the home of the great brahmin Vimalaprabha.
At that time, the World-Honored One’s body, golden in color from top to bottom,
emitted various lights and immeasurable marks,
transforming them into a manifold net of radiant light.
It illuminates all Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions,
and furthermore, it shines upon the assemblies at the sites of enlightenment of all those Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, within those fields.
They transformed themselves into various implements of offering,
illuminated him, and then returned to enter the pores of Śākyamuni’s body.
At that moment, the great Brahmin Vimalaprabha—
Together with their retinue, they were single-mindedly respectful and desired to make offerings to the Buddha;
they swept the roads and adorned them with pure splendor.
At that time, the World-Honored One...
Together with the great assembly of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, Śakra, Brahmā,
and the four world-protecting kings.
Maheśvara, Nārāyaṇa, and a multitude of hundreds of thousands followed in respectful attendance as they proceeded toward him.
At that time, the World-Honored One was walking along the road.
On the road ahead, there was a park named Ananda.
Within that park stood a large, ancient stupa that was extremely dilapidated,
with thorns, weeds, and thickets of forest surrounding it on all sides.
It was solid and obstructed, like a mound of earth.
At that time, as the World-Honored One approached that stūpa,
flames blazed intensely all around the four sides of the mound.
Various forms and colors shone with brilliant light,
visible from both near and far at that ruined stupa;
furthermore, wondrous sounds issued forth from within the light.
He praised him, saying, "Excellent, excellent, Śākyamuni Buddha!
Your pure and subtle auspicious signs are immeasurable and beyond calculation.
That great Brahmin Vimalaprabha then made a request to the Tathāgata.
Now, a rare and inconceivable great event has manifested.
At that time, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni,
desiring to offer worship, circumambulated the stūpa located upon the ruins of the old mound.
He further removed his own garments and ornaments and covered that old stupa mound;
having finished covering it, he wept bitterly, shedding tears like rain.
Furthermore, as he further contemplated the appearance of the śarīra and the simultaneous appearance of all Buddhas of the ten directions,
the śarīra immediately surged forth from the stūpa and came to rest within the palms of the hands of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, throughout the ten directions.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions likewise shed tears.
Those Buddhas emitted light from their bodies,
which illuminated the ancient stupa and formed a net of radiance.
The interior and exterior were transparently radiant and pure beyond compare;
thereafter, the light and the Buddha’s relics returned into the stūpa.
At that time, the assembled multitude—
They all wept with grief;
struck with wonder and marveling at this unprecedented occurrence, they sighed that such a thing had never been seen before.
At that time, within the assembly, there was a great yakṣa lord named Vajrapāṇi.
His body was ablaze with radiance, and his arms were muscular and straight;
they were soft, supple, and lustrous like an elephant’s trunk.
He proceeded with swift motion toward the presence of the World-Honored One, carrying a wheel and a vajra.
Prostrating with his head at the Buddha’s feet, he addressed the Buddha,
saying: "World-Honored One, why do you manifest these rare and wondrous signs of auspiciousness,
such that all the Buddhas of the ten directions shed tears and radiate brilliant light?"
"I only pray that the Tathāgata will expound for me and resolve the doubts of the assembly.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Great Yakṣa Lord Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"This is the collection of the entire bodily relics (śarīra) of all the Tathāgatas within this stūpa."
Furthermore, the images of all Tathāgatas, numbering as many as hundreds of thousands of koṭis of sesame seeds,
as well as the dhāraṇī of the Heart-Seal of the True Dharma, are also within the stūpa. Vajrapāṇi,
you should know that these images of the Buddhas are equal in measure to this quantity of sesame seeds.
The *Saddharmahṛdayamudrādhāraṇī* resides within this stūpa.
Because of this, the bodily relics (*śarīra*) of hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Tathāgatas also abide herein.
If this *Saddharmahṛdayamudrādhāraṇī* is present within this stūpa, [the same applies].
Those eighty-four thousand Dharma-gates are also contained herein;
furthermore, the prophecies conferred upon ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of Tathāgatas from their uṣṇīṣas are also contained herein.
Vajrapāṇi, you should know that the merits of all stūpas containing the relics of the Tathāgatas,
as well as those of this Heart-Seal Dhāraṇī of the True Dharma, are immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and beyond praise.
Vajrapāṇi, you should know that by means of this Heart Dhāraṇī of the Dharma-Casket Seal,
one is able to increase and bring to perfection all true dharmas and all merits.
At that time, when the World-Honored One spoke this Dharma,
the great assembly, having heard the Dharma, rejoiced;
they eliminated their defilements and attained the purity of the Dharma-eye.

Among them, there were those who attained the fruits of stream-entry, once-returning, non-returning, and arhatship, as well as those of the pratyekabuddha vehicle; among them, there were also those who realized the first, second, and even up to the tenth bhūmi.
Among them, some attain the six pāramitās, all of which become perfectly fulfilled;
some receive the prediction of enlightenment (bodhy-avyākaraṇa);
and some attain the stage of non-retrogression (avaivartika).
At that time, the great Brahmin Vimalaprabha,
right there in the assembly, became free from all afflictions;
having extinguished all obstructive defilements, he attained the five supernormal powers.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Yakṣa Lord,
beholding such rare and wondrous manifestations of sovereign supernatural power,
leaped for joy and marveled at this unprecedented occurrence.
And he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, this Heart Dhāraṇī of the Seal of the True Dharma possesses such vast benefits as these."
If sentient beings were to transcribe, adorn, uphold,
recite, and respectfully praise [this],
what would be the fruit of their reward? I pray that the Buddha will explain this.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Great Yakṣa Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively; I shall speak for you.
If there should be bhikṣus or bhikṣuṇīs..."
Upāsakas and upāsikās who receive, uphold,

recite, read, transcribe, and revere this Heart Dhāraṇī of the Seal of the True Dharma shall obtain [the blessings of] as many Tathāgatas in bodily form as there are ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of sesame seeds.
This is the accumulation of merit and the fruit of one’s roots of goodness;
furthermore, one shall encounter and serve those Tathāgatas and receive the prediction of enlightenment. Why is this so?
This Heart Dharani of the Seal of the True Dharma was proclaimed together by as many Tathagatas as there are sesame seeds in nine hundred and ninety million billion nayutas.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who receives, maintains, reads, and recites this *Saddharmamudrā-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,

they will immediately encounter as many Tathāgatas in the form of images as there are sesame seeds in nine million nine hundred thousand *koṭis* of *nayutas* throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs,
upāsakas, upāsikās, sons of noble family,
or daughters of noble family.
Regarding this *Saddharmamudrā-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*,
if one can daily reverently offer flowers, incense,
powdered incense, flower garlands, and ointments;

The merit obtained from [offering] fine garments and ornaments is no different from the merit of making offerings to as many images of Tathāgatas as there are sesame seeds in nine hundred and ninety million *koṭis* throughout the worlds of the ten directions.
Furthermore, he obtained the vast and magnificent ornaments of each and every Tathāgata,
as well as immeasurable heaps of the seven precious gems as large as Mount Sumeru.
At that time, the entire assembly— including devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kinnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and all others— [was present].
They were all struck with wonder and doubt, exclaiming that it was unprecedented:
"How is it that such a decayed and ruined stupa has been so long obstructed by thorns?"
The grasses, trees, and forests are dense and thickly packed, like a mound of earth.
Today, the Tathāgata, out of great compassion and through his sovereign supernormal powers,
manifests such rare and auspicious signs as these inconceivable stupas made of the seven precious jewels.
At that time, the great assembly praised it boundlessly.
Immediately, within the assembly, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Yakṣa Lord,
addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, how is it that you have destroyed this stūpa on the mound and manifested such a multitude of wondrous adornments?
At that time, the Buddha addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
Apart from this stūpa made of mounds and earth that has fallen into ruin,
there is no other stūpa composed of the seven precious gems and various wonders. Why is this so?
Manifesting in accordance with consciousness, one may see stupas made of thorns or mounds of earth,
or see those adorned with the myriad wonders of the seven precious jewels;
furthermore, there are the stupas manifested by the Buddhas which enshrine the bodily relics of the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
Adorned with hundreds of rare treasures, the seven precious gems, and myriad wonders,
sentient beings whose karma is evil perceive it as a ruined stūpa overgrown with thorns.
One should know that this is the Great Yakṣa Lord Vajrapāṇi.
If, during the final period of the末法 (mofa) age,
sentient beings possess deeply grave karmic offenses and fail to plant roots of virtue,
extensively performing unwholesome deeds that lead to the three evil realms.
Due to these causes and conditions, they are born in worlds where no Buddha exists;
they never hear the names of the Buddhas,
and they are perpetually far removed from even the name of the Sangha and the Dharma.
Such matters are true and not false;
for this reason, all Buddhas and I shed tears and lament with sorrow.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi:
When the True Dharma is about to perish, one should abide by this stūpa.
All the whole-body relics of the Tathāgatas are likewise enshrined within this stūpa;
that is to say, they are protected by means of the Dharma taught by all the Tathāgatas.
Thereupon, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Yakṣa Lord, addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, how should all sentient beings plant roots of goodness? How should they establish this stūpa within the True Dharma?"
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Vajrapāṇi,
saying: "Furthermore, if there should be someone who, with faith and understanding, receives, maintains, recites, copies, and explains it to others,
and adorns it in various ways and places it within a stūpa."
That is to say, one shall enshrine within this stūpa the entire bodily relics (sarīra) of all Tathāgatas,
and furthermore, one shall receive the protection of the secret dhāraṇīs of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, they shall obtain the protection of stupas for the images of Buddhas as numerous as ninety-nine sesame seeds from the worlds of the ten directions.
Furthermore, they shall obtain the protection of the Uṣṇīṣa-locana stupas of all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, if there is someone who, using the seven precious gems,
consecrates them according to the Dharma to carve images of various Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
adorning them in every way and enshrining them within a stūpa.
Furthermore, they were adorned with parasols, parasol-rings, jeweled nets, and bells;
with various exquisite ornaments,
as well as bells, chimes, cymbals, gongs, and all manner of ritual vessels.
With flower perfumes, necklaces, garments, food, drink, and all such articles of offering,
and further empowered by the true protection and purification of the sublime Dharma of all Tathāgatas,
one should be diligent at all times, remaining free from indolence.
Furthermore, when this stūpa undergoes change, decay, or destruction,
one should restore it, adorn it, and make various offerings;
with a focused mind of faith and reverence, one should not give rise to doubt or slander.
They shall attain unsurpassed enlightenment.
Furthermore, if there are those who circumambulate this stūpa even once or twice, or perform a single prostration;
One will immediately attain liberation from the sin of immediate retribution and shall certainly realize the stage of *avaivartika*,
until finally reaching the fruit of Buddhahood and Bodhi.
Wherever this stūpa is located, the forms and images of all the Buddhas of the ten directions are also present therein.
Furthermore, wherever this stūpa is located, by the power of the protection of all those Tathāgatas, it is likewise so.
That land is level on all four sides and free from the untimely harm of venomous dragons, thunder, hail, wind, or rain, as well as from all forms of fear.
Furthermore, that place is devoid of various poisonous insects and ants.
That is to say, venomous snakes, wolves, rats, locusts, vipers, scorpions, wasps, and black bees—
even centipedes and millipedes— are all entirely absent. Furthermore,
that land is free from violent and wicked tigers, wolves, and lions.
Flying birds and running beasts cannot cause them harm.
Furthermore, all calamities in that land shall not disturb them, nor shall there be yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, vetālas, or piśācas.
Madness, demonic possession, and malevolent spirits cannot cause them harm.
Furthermore, they shall not suffer from malaria, sores, swellings, skin eruptions, hemorrhoids, fistulas, white leprosy, scabies, or eczema;
no diseases whatsoever shall be able to afflict them.
Furthermore, if there are those who see this jeweled stūpa and joyfully praise and prostrate to it,
they cannot be harmed by various forms of destruction or injury.
Moreover, the various animals of that land— such as oxen, horses, sheep, and dogs— [shall likewise be protected].
Neither men nor women shall suffer untimely death;
nor shall there be any fear of weapons, swords, staves, fire, water, burning, or flooding.
Furthermore, that land shall be free from the various terrors of famine and pestilence.
In that place, one will always be surrounded and protected by the Four Great Heavenly Kings,
as well as the twenty-eight classes of great yakṣa lords,
who constantly come to provide protection while remaining hidden in their forms and appearances.
As well as the Heaven of the Thirty-three, the twenty-eight lunar mansions, Rāhu, and all the stars;
even down to the sun and moon moving in their proper courses through day and night;
and if the various dragon kings constantly observe and cause rain to fall at the appropriate times.
Furthermore, there may be all the devas of the desire realm, the form realm, and even the formless realm,
who descend upon this stūpa at the three times of day to prostrate, make offerings, and pay homage;
they are all revered, honored, remembered, and contemplated by all Tathāgatas.
Furthermore, if there are those who constantly cultivate the adornment of Buddha-stūpas and images—
whether using wood, stone, clay, paint, gold, silver, brass, or other materials—
and likewise transcribe and adorn this *Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Seal of the Heart of the True Dharma*, [they shall attain these benefits].
Furthermore, having been protected according to the Dharma by all Tathāgatas,
it was then placed within a precious stūpa.
Moreover, the stairways on all four sides of this precious stūpa were entirely and magnificently adorned.
The *cakra-cchattra* (wheel-pinnacle), banners, and streamers were encircled by hanging bells;
nets of the seven precious gems, high, wide, large, and small,
were adorned in various ways according to one's wishes with complete mastery.
Furthermore, one should empower it with the True Dharma of the Tathāgatas of the ten directions.
One should then provide protection by performing the rites for the guardianship of all the holy sages.
Thereafter, one should reverently make extensive offerings of various incenses, flowers, food, and drink, up to and including necklaces and ornaments.
In this way, one obtains immeasurable merit.
At that moment, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Yakṣa Lord, was present in the assembly and again addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, by what causes and conditions does this come to pass?"
By copying, receiving, upholding, making offerings to, and revering this Heart Dhāraṇī of the Seal of the True Dharma,
one obtains such immeasurable merits as these.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"This is the Heart Dhāraṇī of the Secret Casket Seal of the Relics of the Entire Body of All Tathāgatas of the Dharma Realm."
Thus one obtains these immeasurable merits.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the great yakṣa lord,
heard of the immeasurable merits spoken by the Buddha.
Rejoicing and receiving it with faith, they addressed the Buddha again, saying:
"World-Honored One, we pray that the Buddha, out of his great compassion, will expound this Dharma;
we long to hear it."
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Listen attentively; I shall now speak for you this Heart Dhāraṇī of the Seal of the True Dharma."
This has been proclaimed in common by all Buddhas of the past, future, and present. If there are those who believe and accept it, and who respectfully make offerings to it,
they shall eventually realize and enter the states of the Śrāvaka, Pratyekabuddha, and the Dharma-body, Reward-body, and Transformation-body of the ten stages.
Therefore, it is named the "Seal of the Secret Casket of the Perfectly Complete True Dharma.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this mantra: *Namaḥ siddhye vikānāṃ sarvadharmāṇām*.
Oṃ caturvidha-siddhi-pavana-vare vavare julu julu tara tara sarva-tathāgata-dhātu-tarale padma-sambhave jaya-taralambaje samaradanta-makara-pramardani svāhā.

Sajjihvāmūlīya-vat-khaṭa-ṭheṭhiṭha 31. Dhaḥ-tu-jihvāmūlīya-bhe svāhā 32. Camakāya ṭheṭhide svāhā 33. Sarvatathāgata 34. Hrīṇadhaḥtumudari svāhā.
Hāḥ (35) apratihatastutibhiḥ (36) tathāgatadhiṣṭhite (37) hulu hulu hūṃ hūṃ svāhā (38) oṃ (39) sarvatathāgatoṣṇīṣatejomālini (40) udāre...
HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ SVĀHĀ. (41) SARVATATHĀGATA-DṚṢṬI-VIŚODHANI HŪṂ HŪṂ HŪṂ SVĀHĀ. (42–44) At that time, having spoken this mantra, the World-Honored One addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
This Heart Dharani of the Secret Casket Seal of the Entire Body has been universally proclaimed by all Tathagatas throughout every direction of the ten worlds.
There were ninety-nine hundred thousand koṭis of nāyutas of Tathāgatas, each with a physical form the size of ninety-nine sesame seeds;
having heard this Dharma being taught, they all came to this place.
They all praised him together, saying:
"Excellent, excellent, Śākyamuni!
You have skillfully expounded the Dhāraṇī of the Seal of the Mind from the Casket of the True Dharma."
He caused it to be widely circulated and practiced throughout Jambudvīpa.
Furthermore, he caused all sentient beings to enshrine the bodily relics within this stūpa.
By virtue of this, all Tathāgatas of the ten directions shall protect and sustain them through various samādhis.
Furthermore, if there be any person who receives, upholds, reads, recites, explains, or transcribes this *Sarvaśarīra-guhya-peṭaka-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, [they shall likewise be so protected].
Furthermore, when [the image] is adorned with gold, silver, sandalwood, carvings, and colors, and installed within a stūpa,
all Tathāgatas of the worlds of the ten directions will constantly come here to bestow their protective empowerment upon it.
At that time, when the World-Honored One was preaching this Dhāraṇī of the Heart-Seal of the Dharma-Casket,
a subtle stupa made of the seven treasures emerged from within the old, dilapidated mound.
Adorned with various kinds of *cakra*, banners, and streamers,
the great assembly of humans and devas all beheld it;
it remained manifest as before for a long time.
At that time, the assembly of great bodhisattvas and śrāvakas,
as well as the eight classes of beings— gods, nāgas, and others, both human and non-human—
all beheld this marvel and were filled with joy.
At that time, when the World-Honored One was preaching this Dharma,
the great assembly, including Vajrapāṇi, the Great Yakṣa Lord;
and the Brahmin Vimalaprabha, [were present].
Together with all the bodhisattvas and great śrāvakas,
as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and so forth.
The king, ministers, elders, householders,
and the entire assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken,
received it with single-minded faith and withdrew with joy.
The Dhāraṇī Sūtra of the Heart-Seal of the Secret Casket of the True Dharma of All Tathāgatas.
